page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture instance within the e2 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs, mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.2 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the e2-highmem-4 is positioned in the lower tiers for compute-heavy tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance benchmarks rank in the bottom 25%, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently register in the bottom 25%, though the PassMark memory score achieves an average rating in the middle 50%. Text and image processing, along with static web serving throughput, are also positioned in the bottom 10% of tested servers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high memory capacity relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute capabilities. The hardware configuration is suitable for small-scale database operations, caching layers, and lightweight text generation tasks, where the 102.59 tokens per second average performance on small language model text generation can be utilized without incurring the costs of higher-tier compute-optimized hardware.
